name: Synthetic agents as models of human values
description: Using LLMs as synthetic survey respondents or cultural agents; whether aggregate anchors can reproduce real population attitudes; limits and validity of silicon samples.

name: Formal verification for economics
description: Lean 4 and theorem proving applied to economic theory, mechanism design and equilibrium proofs; machine-checked guarantees instead of informal arguments.

name: AI and journalism
description: How AI changes newsrooms and reporting; deepfakes, misinformation, synthetic media, editorial standards, and press-freedom organisations' responses.

name: AI in education
description: AI tutors, lesson design, teacher workflows, learning evidence and what makes AI-generated lessons actually useful in classrooms.

name: Measurement and construct validity with LLMs
description: Whether LLM-based measures of social-science constructs (trust, values, attitudes) measure what they claim; psychometrics, benchmarks, evaluation design.

name: Economics of AI and productivity
description: Macro and labor effects of AI adoption, productivity paradox, institutions, and what the evidence does and does not show.

name: Automated research and AI agents for science
description: Agentic research workflows, reproducibility, human-in-the-loop research tooling, and the reliability of autonomous research pipelines.

name: Latin American economy and institutions
description: Argentina and the region: macro policy, inflation, institutional quality, and how technology and AI interact with development.

name: Culture, norms and technology
description: How culture and preferences shape technology adoption, and how AI systems encode or flatten cultural differences.

name: Causal inference
description: Identification strategies, RCTs, econometrics, DAGs, synthetic control and difference-in-differences; how credible causal claims are from observational data, experiments and ML-based estimators.

name: Complexity science and the Santa Fe Institute
description: Complex adaptive systems, agent-based models, emergence, scaling laws and network science; research, people and ideas from the Santa Fe Institute.
